patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient is a retired professional athlete who has been experiencing bilateral wrist and knee pain for the last 10 years. He reports morning stiffness in his joints lasting about 50 minutes but denies any joint swelling, color changes in digits, or dryness of mucous membranes. He also denies any constitutional symptoms such as fever or chills.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: History of being a professional athlete. No significant past medical history reported.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Retired, does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with long-term bilateral wrist and knee pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Hello, doctor. I’ve had bilateral wrist and knee pain for about 10 years, with morning stiffness that lasts roughly 50 minutes. I don’t notice any joint swelling, color changes in my fingers, dry mouth/eyes, or any fever or chills.”
Can you tell me your age and gender?
“Sure, doctor—I’m a 55-year-old male.”
Have you noticed any skin rashes, particularly
“No, doctor, I haven’t noticed any skin rashes or any new bumps on my skin.”
Have you noticed any changes in your fingernails, such
“No changes in my fingernails, doctor—no pitting, lifting, or discoloration that I’ve noticed.”
Have you had any back pain, particularly pain that wakes you
“No, doctor—I've not really had significant back pain, and nothing that seems to wake me up at night due to pain.”
Have you noticed any grinding, clicking, or popping sounds in

“No, doctor—I haven’t really noticed grinding, clicking, or popping sounds in my joints. The main issue for me has been the persistent bilateral wrist and knee pain along with the morning stiffness lasting about 50 minutes.”
Have you ever been told you have any other medical conditions
“No, doctor—I've not been told I have any other medical conditions. I’m generally healthy otherwise, aside from the long-standing bilateral wrist and knee pain and the morning stiffness.”
Have you noticed any fatigue, changes in your skin color

“No, doctor—I haven’t noticed unusual fatigue beyond my baseline, and I haven’t seen any changes in my skin color. It’s mostly the long-standing wrist and knee pain with the morning stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes.”
Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits
“No, doctor—my bowel habits haven’t changed noticeably, and I haven’t had any new diarrhea, constipation, or blood in my stool.”
Have you ever had any sexually transmitted infections, or
“No, doctor—I’ve never been told I had a sexually transmitted infection. I don’t have any genital sores, discharge, or other symptoms that would suggest an STI.”
Have you had any previous injuries or trauma to your wrists or

“No, doctor—during my athletic career I had the usual minor overuse issues, but I haven’t had any specific major trauma or fractures to my wrists. The pain has just gradually persisted in both wrists and both knees over the last 10 years.”
Have you noticed any muscle weakness, particularly when trying to
“No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any specific muscle weakness in my wrists or knees. My main problem is the persistent pain with morning stiffness lasting about 50 minutes.”
Have you noticed if the pain gets worse with activity and better

“Doctor, the pain tends to be worse in the morning and does improve as I get moving, but it can flare again with prolonged activity or overuse. Rest helps somewhat, but the stiffness and aching usually return after I’ve been sitting still.”
Have you ever had any blood tests or x

“Doctor, I’ve had some blood tests in the past but I don’t remember the exact results, and I haven’t had anything that clearly changed the diagnosis. I’ve also had X-rays of my wrists and knees years ago, but they didn’t give me a definitive answer.”
Have you noticed any nodules or lumps under your skin,
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any nodules, lumps under my skin, or any unusual bumps—just the ongoing bilateral wrist and knee pain with the morning stiffness that lasts about 50 minutes.”
